pages.title: What this unit is about
pages.body:
> 🧩 **Strand 4 — Computational Thinking**
Sub-strand 4: Artificial Intelligence

How does a machine’s “intelligence” compare with a human’s or a dog’s? In this unit you will look inside artificial neural networks, compare intelligence in humans, animals and machines, and explore holograms and mixed reality.

pages.title: ANNs; Human, Animal and Machine Intelligence; Holograms
Comparing intelligence
pages.body:
## Comparing intelligence
| **Aspect** | **Humans** | **Animals** | **Machines (AI)** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Learning | Learn from experience, teaching, reading; abstract reasoning | Learn mainly from experience and instinct; some learn tricks | Learn from large amounts of data; need training |
| Speed and memory | Limited memory; slower calculation | Limited | Huge memory; very fast calculation |
| Creativity and emotion | Highly creative; feelings, empathy, morals | Some emotions (fear, affection); limited creativity | No real feelings; can generate content by copying patterns |
| Common sense and adaptability | Strong; adapt to new situations | Adapt within their environment | Weak; struggle with situations unlike their training |
| Senses | Five senses integrated | Some senses stronger than humans (dogs’ smell, bats’ echolocation) | Sensors and cameras; can “see” infrared, etc. |
| Tiredness and consistency | Get tired, make errors | Get tired | Work 24/7 consistently, but errors can repeat at scale |
| Energy use | Brain uses about 20 watts | Low | Training large AI uses enormous amounts of electricity |
> 🧪 **Activity — Capabilities and limitations**
In groups with assigned roles (leader, recorder, presenter, timekeeper), list three tasks humans do better than machines, three tasks machines do better than humans, and three tasks animals do better than both. Present your list.

pages.title: Strong AI vs weak AI
pages.body:
## Strong AI vs weak AI
| **Weak (narrow) AI** | **Strong (general) AI** |
|---|---|
| Designed for **one specific task** or a limited range of tasks | Would have **general intelligence** equal to or greater than humans across any task |
| Exists today: voice assistants, face recognition, chess programs, chatbots, self-driving systems | Does **not yet exist**; it is a research goal and a subject of debate |
| Does not truly understand or have consciousness | Would understand, reason, plan and possibly be self-aware |
## Holograms and mixed reality
A **hologram** is a three-dimensional image formed by recording and recreating the pattern of light waves reflected from an object. In true holography, a **laser** beam is split in two: one beam lights the object, the other goes directly to the recording surface, and the **interference pattern** of the two beams is recorded. When light shines on the recording, a 3D image appears that changes as you move your head. Holograms are used as security features on bank cards, banknotes and passports.
**Mixed Reality (MR)** headsets such as **Microsoft HoloLens** project holographic-looking 3D objects into your real surroundings, which you can walk around and interact with, for example a 3D heart for a biology lesson or a machine part for an engineer. Many stage “holograms” of performers are actually optical illusions (such as Pepper’s ghost) rather than true holograms.

2. Compare human, animal and machine intelligence under **three** headings.
